messages.author: df51387064954b5e
messages.subject: Error fitting dsm in R
parts:
Hello everybody!

I'm Paula and I'm performing my Distance analysis in R (R version 3.3.2 (2016-10-31)) to analyse cetacean abundance and distribution from line-transect surveys. Therefore, in order to perform that analysis I'm also using the following R packages:
- dsm_2.2.15
- Distance_0.9.7
- gam_1.14-4
- mgcv_1.8-15

When fitting dsm I get an strange error, that didn't appear last year when I performed the same analysis with the same formulas. I was wondering if anyone has had the same problem or someone know how can I fix it (because it seems to be a problem of my R packages versions).
The formula I use to fit the dsm is:

dsm_depth <- dsm(count~s(Bathy), ddf.obj=hn.beau, segment.data = segdata, observation.data=obsdata, family=nb(), method="REML")

The error I get when run the code is the following:

Count model with detection function covariates at the segment level: this is EXPERIMENTAL!
Error in predict.ds(ddfobject, newdata = nd) : 
  fields or factor levels in `newdata` do not match data used in fitted model


In addition, I tried the same model but simplifying the detection function (just in case...) not adding to it any covariate. In this case, R fits the model but when I call the summary of the model "summary(dsm_depth)" I get another error:

Error in qr.lm(object) : lm object does not have a proper 'qr' component.
 Rank zero or should not have used lm(.., qr=FALSE).

I have read that this last error may be caused by not loading the gam or mgcv packages, but I have loaded both... 



Any help would be very welcome since I have read some documents, tried a lot of things and found nothing that could help me.

Thank you everyone in advance and happy weekend!

Paula.

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error fitting dsm in R
parts:
Hi Paula, hi listfolk,

The former issue I think is easier to diagnose: if you have a covariate
in the detection function and you use count as the response in the DSM,
you must have a column in your segment data for that covariate. For
example if you include Beaufort sea state as a covariate in your
detection function, you must also have Beaufort sea state measured at
each segment.

The second error I am not sure about, if you are able to email me the
saved model object off-list I will look into it.


cheers,
--dave

Hi again and thank you for your answer David!

Although I have bad news... I have checked it and I have already a column called "beaufort" in my segment data with the data for each segment, as well as I have it in the distdata used to fit the detection function. So, do you know what else may be causing that error?

About the second error, it is an odd thing. I have saved the model in rds format to send it to you but first I tried to read it in R again. Well, when I called the model (using readRDS) and tried to make the summary... It worked!! But if I try to make the summary of the model itself it doesn't works....
As you can imagine it's a waste of time save all the possible models like this and then open them again. Any suggestion?
Should I attach the rds file here or should I send it to you by email?

Thank you again and sorry for these odd things!
Paula.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error fitting dsm in R
parts:
Hi there again!

An update of my problems for anyone who could be interested. The second problem was probably caused by "masking" between packages and was easily fixed not loading gam or gmcv when loading dsm and Distance packages.

But I still have problems fitting a dsm using a detection function with covariables. As I said, my segment data have a column for the covariate that I'm using, so I don´t know what is causing the problem. I tried to eliminate that column from my segment data to check what the error would be. It is the following:
Count model with detection function covariates at the segment level: this is EXPERIMENTAL!

Error in make.data(response, ddf.obj, segment.data, observation.data,  : 
  Detection function covariates are not in the segment data
  Missing: size

But the problem I get is different (when the covariate of the detection function is in the segment data). It seems that has something to do with the calculation of the predictions. It is the following:

Count model with detection function covariates at the segment level: this is EXPERIMENTAL!
Error in predict.ds(ddfobject, newdata = nd) : 
  fields or factor levels in `newdata` do not match data used in fitted model

Any suggestion or advice?

Thank you in advance!
Paula.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error fitting dsm in R
parts:
Paula

I'm trying to interpret the error messages you are receiving.  I note the covariate of interest is "size", which I presume is size of animal cluster.  If so, that should not be information stored at the segment level of your data, but rather at the observation level of your data.  The cluster size should be associated with each of your detections, not the segments.
